key_insight: Laya-IsoToken enables clinical codebook switching without target-labeled training notes by separating clinical text reading from code definitions.
clinical_relevance: The approach could reduce reannotation burden when hospitals change coding systems or deploy coding across languages.
method: Train a clinical span reader once using source records and a frozen multilingual concept space.
Compile public target-code descriptions into alignment operators in under three seconds.
Route unfamiliar concepts to offline language-model verification using a geometric residual.
evidence_signal: Across 32,804 ICD-9 and 13,783 unseen-patient ICD-10 discharges, the abstract reports 62.6% source Micro-F1 and a 5.4-point ICD-10 F1 gain over semantic crosswalks; offline verification on 1,000 summaries achieved 40.6% ICD-10 Micro-F1 with no invalid codes observed.
watch_item: Real-world generalizability and workflow impact require prospective validation; zero invalid codes does not mean all assigned codes were correct.
paper_title: Laya-IsoToken: Day-One Clinical Codebook Switching via Closed-Form Operator Compilation
